narrative: The PR ran to the five-round cap, and most later findings trace to three fixes. F3's one-site comment fix left five sibling comments to be re-found one per round, and even the declared sweep (F12) missed config-hint.ts. F4's barrel fix in check.ts did not grep for the same reach-past in protocol.ts (three duplicate threads). F11's `present()` boolean regressed the collision detector (F16) and then the full chain (F21-F23). Its second redesign added an `unreadable` arm and an `unchecked` list that produced round 4's dedupe bug and two stale-doc findings. Round 4 (and so the uncapped round 5) consisted entirely of fix-caused findings.
guidance_observations: Single-site fixes to a staleness class (comment enumerating sources, barrel bypass) were the dominant cost; a grep-everything sweep on the first finding would have removed eight later findings.

The F11 redesign was made under pressure in one round and needed two further rounds to converge; enumerating how each caller consumes a three-way probe before writing it would have landed the final design first.
Round-4 replies were bare 'Fixed in 5900a67' with no plan or verification, so the fixes went unreviewed because of the round cap.

narrative: A wizard rewrite drew three round-0 findings: one real missing-glyph bug fixed, and two well-founded pushbacks against silent fallbacks. Round 1 found real wizard-flow defects (install ordering, the skipped-settings outcome, backup clobbering, the eager-lookup crash), all fixed with sound designs. Round 2's three findings were S1-S3: two were pre-existing text the flag misattributed to the candybar.md fix commit, and one was a mis-stated stream in a comment the F7 fix introduced. Round 3 came back clean.
guidance_observations: The pushbacks (F2, F3, F8) were argued from concrete contracts rather than preference, and none resurfaced.
Fix commits were verified live (timings for the deadline loop, xxd for glyphs), and nothing regressed except one wrong comment.
